description: Difficulty ratings (0-10 per criterion, plus a length-weighted final score) for every aliyah and for each parsha as a whole. Generated with a transparent rule-based methodology, NOT a survey of actual leining outcomes -- see difficulty-rubric.md for the full methodology (including the length weighting and the 'known leining' familiarity discount), the content-profile tags used, and honest caveats about where this should be refined (e.g. with real chazzanim feedback or app usage data).

aliyot.note: Ends with Birkat Kohanim (Num 6:24-26), recited daily by kohanim and heard weekly by the whole congregation during duchening -- familiar, though it is only the tail of a long aliyah otherwise dominated by the (unfamiliar) sotah and nazir laws.
Start of the 12 nearly-identical Nesiim offerings (Num 7:1-41) -- easy to lose your place
Nesiim offerings continue (Num 7:42-71) -- near-identical repeated text
Nesiim offerings conclude (Num 7:72-89) -- near-identical repeated text
Eisav's genealogy begins (Gen 36:1-19) -- unfamiliar names
Eisav's genealogy concludes (Gen 36:20-43) -- long list of unfamiliar names
Contains a shalshelet (Lev 8:23, miluim blood on Aharon's ear)
Journey-stations list begins (Num 33:1-10)
Bulk of the 42 journey-stations list (Num 33:11-49) -- long place-name list
Ends with the third paragraph of the Shema / the tzitzit passage (Num 15:37-41), recited twice daily -- widely known by heart, though it is only the tail of this aliyah.
Contains a shalshelet (Gen 19:16, Lot lingers) -- a trope mark used only 4x in the whole Torah

Aseret HaDibrot repeated (Deut 5:6-18) -- ta'am elyon in many congregations The Aseret HaDibrot are also one of the most familiar passages in the Torah -- this softens the vocabulary/unfamiliarity difficulty even though the ta'am elyon trope override above still applies in full.

Contains the Shema and V'ahavta (Deut 6:4-9), recited twice daily -- most regular daveners already know this passage by heart, which offsets much of the unfamiliarity-driven difficulty (the words still must be read correctly from the text, not recited from memory).

Shirat HaYam / Az Yashir (Ex 15:1-19) -- special brick-layout & elevated melody Az Yashir is recited daily in Pesukei D'Zimra -- most daveners know the words well, though that familiarity doesn't fully prepare a reader to lead its special trope solo.
The 12 curses of Har Eival (Deut 27:15-26) -- repetitive "cursed be... amen" refrain
Tochacha (curses, Deut 28:15-68) -- traditional custom to read quickly and quietly; the longest aliyah in the Torah by verse count
Includes the archaic poetic fragment "Az Yashir Yisrael" and a quote from the Book of the Wars of Hashem
Tochacha (curses, Lev 26:14-46) -- traditional custom to read quickly and quietly
Opening of Shirat Ha'azinu -- poetic column layout

Aseret HaDibrot (Ex 20:2-14) -- ta'am elyon alternate cantillation The Aseret HaDibrot are also one of the most familiar passages in the Torah -- this softens the vocabulary/unfamiliarity difficulty even though the ta'am elyon trope override above still applies in full.
Contains the second paragraph of the Shema (Deut 11:13-21), recited twice daily -- widely known by heart.
Contains a shalshelet (Gen 24:12, Eliezer prays)
Contains a shalshelet (Gen 39:8, Yosef refuses)
